definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese straight-sleeved coat, typically worn during festivals, by shop workers, or as a uniform. Made of cotton or other lightweight fabric, often bearing the crest or name of a group, shrine, or business on the back.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{法被|はっぴ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
examples.english: To wear a happi coat at a festival.

examples.japanese: ⟦{背中|せなか}→背中：00810_senaka⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{町名|ちょうめい}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧{法被|はっぴ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}た→着る：00541_kiru⟧。
examples.english: I wore a happi coat with the neighborhood name on the back.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたち⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧おそろい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{法被|はっぴ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}て→着る：00541_kiru⟧⟦{神輿|みこし}→神輿：10605_mikoshi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担|かつ}いだ→担ぐ：03917_katsugu⟧。
examples.english: The children wore matching happi coats and carried the portable shrine.

notes:
USAGE:
A happi coat is a loose, straight-sleeved jacket, usually hip-length, traditionally worn open in front or tied with a sash. It is most strongly associated with Japanese festivals (⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧), where groups wear matching happi coats to show their affiliation.

Historically also worn by firefighters, shop workers, and craftsmen as a kind of uniform, with the employer's name or crest on the back.

Also written as {半被|はっぴ} or in hiragana as はっぴ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {法被|はっぴ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{着|き}る→着る：00541_kiru⟧: to wear a happi coat
- おそろい⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{法被|はっぴ}: matching happi coats
- ⟦{祭|まつ}り→祭り：03735_matsuri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{法被|はっぴ}: festival happi coat
- {法被|はっぴ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{背中|せなか}→背中：00810_senaka⟧: the back of a happi coat (where crests/names appear)
